reviews.text: A valuable prayer tool to deepen your practice. Best app ever. I have been using it for years and it frames my centering prayer. I love the diverse offerings of prayer to open and close the session. The timer, the bells, all of it. It is a turnkey operation making it easy for people who want to deepen their relationship with God through this beautiful practice.

Simple Focus. This app has helped me practice silence and sense the intimacy of my relationship with God. It’s very simple as should silence be. 

There’s an opening reading that you get to choose: anything from a scripture to a prayer to a spiritual writing by classical authors. Then comes the sound to indicate the beginning of the time of silence. I chose the bell/gong sound. It makes me feel I’m at a monastery. Then comes the time of silence. Sheer silence for an amount of time you’ve chosen. The sound that started the time ends the time and there’s a closing reading of your choice. 

It’s simple but effective. I’m so glad I have this app. So helpful for me to develop this rhythm of silence and solitude with the Lord.

Centering Prayer. I have found the app a very useful aid in my CP practice. If you don’t know CP, it is simply meditation where when you become aware of a thought, you release it, by the use of a short word, silently spoken. Some people use breath or an image instead. And then there is another layer, the concept that you are by this means aware, gradually, that you are “in God”. Usually this is understood in Christian terms, but really, since in Centering Prayer, we release all images or ideas of “God”, it is applicable to any religion, even a spiritual practice that does not involve a deity of any kind, but is just a practice of pure awareness. 

But the app is specifically Christian, so if that isn’t your tradition, it won’t be helpful for you, most likely. There are many books on CP, just do a search. Thomas Keating’s are foundational, then Cynthia Bourgeault, and David Frenette.

I was part of a centering prayer group at a church I attended so I was familiar with it - I simply call it Christian meditation - and I was eager to try out the app. So happy to say that it does not disappoint! In fact it's wonderful. It adds prayers at the beginning and end of your meditation if you want them but you can also choose to forego them, too. You can choose the sounds at the beginning and end of the session too - I have remained with the sounds of gongs (like the sounds of a meditation bowl) but there are other choices, too, including Gregorian chants. 

You can customize a lot and find a nice rhythm for a more Christian flavor of a meditation practice, or as a way to deepen and expand your current prayer practice. 

The only addition I would like is a section to make a brief note of a day's session. My old meditation app did have this and it was useful. 

Otherwise it is a lovely app and I am glad I discovered it.
